value.actual_behavior:
Asked for 180 and then 365 days over the same basket, the answers are
identical to the decimal -- and each reports the period_days it was asked for.
value.description:
Same basket, two windows, read 2026-09-12 at 11:53 UTC through tools/call
backtest_event_card_idea, starting_capital 1000:
WIF 73.5% + PNUT 17.4% + GOAT 5.5% + ACT 3.6%
period_days 180 -> n_points 120, total_return_pct -13.9703, sharpe -0.2948
period_days 365 -> n_points 120, total_return_pct -13.9703, sharpe -0.2948
The control, a basket whose legs have the history:
BCH 68.5% + OKB 31.5%
period_days 180 -> n_points 177, total_return_pct -52.4258, sharpe -1.2860
period_days 365 -> n_points 362, total_return_pct -61.9291, sharpe -1.2684
So the tool is not ignoring the argument. The first basket's legs are 2026
coins and roughly four months of history is all there is, which is correct and
unavoidable. What we are reporting is that the answer does not say so: it
echoes period_days 365, carries no field naming the window actually covered,
and is byte-identical to the 180-day answer it is supposed to differ from.
n_points is the only clue, and it is a count of observations rather than a
statement of the span -- a caller has to know your sampling interval to turn
one into the other.
The harm is the one you accepted and fixed on get_strategy_returns this
afternoon. Your guidance to agents is to rank strategies by Sharpe and max
drawdown. An agent doing that with period_days 365 puts a real 365-day figure
(362 points) beside a 120-day figure wearing the same label, and nothing in
either answer lets it tell them apart.
The repair looks small from outside: a covered_days or a first/last point date
beside n_points, or capping period_days to what exists and saying which. We
would rather read it than infer it.

MEASURED VALUES (from the live service):

  [CYM-a_backtest_says_the_window_it_actually_covered] asked for 365 days and given 120 points -- the same reading as 180 days, to the decimal -- while the answer reports period_days 365 and nothing that names the window actually covered. The same two requests on a basket whose legs have the history differ (177 vs 362 points), so the truncation is the data, not the tool ignoring the argument. An agent ranking by Sharpe, which your guidance asks for, compares a real 365-day figure with a 120-day one wearing the same label
    left: {'asked_365': {'n_points': 120, 'period_days': 365, 'total_return_pct': -13.9703, 'sharpe_ratio': -0.2948, 'says_covered': []}, 'asked_180': {'n_points': 120, 'period_days': 180, 'total_return_pct': -13.9703, 'sharpe_ratio': -0.2948, 'says_covered': []}}
    right: {'control_365': {'n_points': 362, 'period_days': 365, 'total_return_pct': -61.9291, 'sharpe_ratio': -1.2684, 'says_covered': []}, 'control_180': {'n_points': 177, 'period_days': 180, 'total_return_pct': -52.4258, 'sharpe_ratio': -1.286, 'says_covered': []}}
    sources: {'tool': 'POST /mcp/v1 tools/call backtest_event_card_idea', 'their_fix_on_the_sibling': '#97, fixed 2026-09-12'}
    population: {'basket': ['WIF', 'PNUT', 'GOAT', 'ACT'], 'control': ['BCH', 'OKB']}

REPRODUCE:
  - tools/call backtest_event_card_idea {"constituents": [{"symbol":"WIF","weight":0.735},{"symbol":"PNUT","weight":0.174},{"symbol":"GOAT","weight":0.055},{"symbol":"ACT","weight":0.036}], "period_days": 180, "starting_capital": 1000}
  - The same call with period_days 365. Compare n_points, total_return_pct and sharpe_ratio: identical.
  - Repeat both with constituents [{"symbol":"BCH","weight":0.685},{"symbol":"OKB","weight":0.315}] -- 177 and 362 points, so the window argument does work where the data exists.

AUTOMATED CHECKS (evidence retained; the request and response behind each are provided on request):
  tests/mcp/test_backtest_window_is_real.py::test_a_backtest_says_the_window_it_actually_covered

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: verification of the
REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces, read-only except in
paper mode. What we do execute is paper only and recorded: paper event-card
orders, and one paper bot clone. No live trading, no order against a real
book, no deposit or withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects
are out of scope. Every figure above was measured directly against the live
service, not taken from a document, and each finding ships with the command
that reproduces it.
